item.title: "He was genial, he was compassionate": Al Michaels gives moving tribute to Dan Hicks
item.description: Credit: Prime Video The sports world spent much of Thursday mourning the sudden death of longtime NBC Sports commentator Dan Hicks at the age of 64. Hicks was known as the lead voice of NBC Sports’s coverage of the PGA Tour, as well as his work with Notre Dame football, and several Olympic sports including swimming and skiing. He was married to fellow veteran broadcaster Hannah Storm. Tributes poured in for Hicks from around the sports world all day , and just after halftime of Thursday Night Football on Prime Video between the New York Giants and Washington Commanders, Al Michaels took a moment to honor his fellow broadcaster. “Well, all of us in the sports broadcasting business were shocked to learn this morning of the passing of Dan Hicks,” Michaels said. “Dan joined NBC Sports in 1992, provided captions to so many iconic moments in golf, tennis, and Notre Dame football, and he and Rowdy Gaines turned the calling of swimming at multiple Olympics into an art form. He was genial. He was compassionate. He was great company, had a world-class sense of humor. On this very rough day for so many of us, we send our love to Hannah and your three daughters. Wishing you strength and comfort.” Michaels’s voice cracked a bit when saying Hannah’s name. Al Michaels gets choked up during a tribute for Dan Hicks on Prime Video’s Thursday Night Football broadcast. https://t.co/yPlnxlDWGW — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 13, 2026 Michaels and Hicks are part of a small group at the top of announcing whose most infamous calls are known in the hearts of sports fans, even if they have no direct knowledge of it. For Michaels, it is the “Do you believe in miracles? Yes!” call from the 1980 Winter Olympics . For Hicks, it was the incredible line, “Expect anything different?!” as Tiger Woods rolled in a 12-foot putt at the 2008 U.S. Open to force a playoff at Torrey Pines. Woods would win the third U.S. Open of his career on the following day. He was also on the call of the Men’s 4x100m Freestyle Relay at the 2008 Olympics as Michael Phelps was looking to make history with eight gold medals in eight events. It was just the second of Phelps’ eight events, and while all eyes entered the race on him, it was an incredible anchor leg from Jason Lezak that won gold, with Lezak making up tons of ground against the favorites France over the final few meters to win at the touch. Phelps would go on to win his eight gold medals, but he never would have had the chance if not for that thrilling closing leg. item.title: Oregon has 3 quarterbacks who could start Saturday. Illinois has a freshman who's never started before
item.description: The Oregon Ducks will face a team on Saturday with an even less desirable quarterback situation. Illinois (3-3, 1-2 Big Ten) quarterback Katin Houser suffered a broken hand that will sideline him for four to six weeks during a 38-37 overtime win over Michigan State on Oct. 10. Oregon has played its last two games without starting quarterback Dante Moore, who suffered a concussion in the second quarter of the Ducks’ 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. However, while Oregon can turn to junior Dylan Raiola — a Nebraska transfer with 23 career starts — and senior Brock Thomas, Illinois is relying on freshman quarterback Michael Clayton II, who will make his first start against the Ducks. A positive for Illinois is that Houser was injured before the team’s bye week, giving coach Bret Bielema two weeks to prepare Clayton. “It was just good timing,” Bielema told reporters during his Monday media session. Illinois is off to a disappointing start after going 9-4 in 2025 and 10-3 in 2024. The defense is below average, while the passing combination of Houser and wide receiver Collin Dixon is one of the nation’s best. Dixon is tied for third nationally with nine touchdown receptions. Illinois head coach Bret Bielema celebrates their overtime win over Michigan State as he walks off the field after an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026, in East Lansing, Mich. (AP Photo/Lon Horwedel) AP Photo/Lon Horwedel AP Photo/Lon Horwedel Now Illinois heads into Saturday’s game against a resurgent Oregon defense, trying to get Clayton up to speed. His performance against MSU elevated expectations. Houser left the game late in the third quarter with Illinois leading 23-10. Clayton completed 6 of 8 passes for 88 yards and two touchdowns. The final touchdown came in overtime on a 25-yard pass that put Illinois up 38-31. Sophomore quarterback Carson Boyd also played. He rushed once for seven yards but did not attempt a pass. Bielema and offensive coordinator Barry Lunney Jr. both said Boyd could play against Oregon (4-2, 2-1), but Clayton is the starter. Usually, Bielema said, his starting quarterback gets a lot of rest during the bye week while the staff works on player development. Given Clayton and Boyd’s inexperience, both got valuable reps in practice last week. “I think those two guys in particular took advantage of every rep,” Bielema said. Bielema has leaned heavily on transfer quarterbacks during his six years at Illinois, including Houser. But that could change if Clayton, a former three-star recruit, earns the job. “I’ve said several times that hopefully the next starter comes from within our program,” Bielema said. Lunney said Clayton will be more prepared than he has in the past given the circumstances. item.title: Reeling Oregon Ducks remain positive, committed to the grind
item.description: EUGENE — The 2026 season is on the verge of completely unraveling for the Oregon Ducks . One more loss, and any shred of postseason hopes would be extinguished. Yet even after two upset losses and falling out of the rankings — despite starting the season at No. 2 — the Ducks (3-2, 1-1 Big Ten) remain focused, together and committed to salvaging the season. “One thing I really love is the way the people in the locker room have been responding to this adversity,” sophomore cornerback Brandon Finney Jr. said. After his team’s 17-15 loss to No. 12 UCLA on Saturday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning said the team would be measured by how it responds moving forward. On Wednesday, he said the team has elevated its work ethic and embraced accountability. “I’ve been proud of the way that they’ve worked,” Lanning said. “I don’t see a lot of hanging heads, right? I think that’s challenging, too, especially when you’re young, to not lose a little bit of gusto and not lose a little bit of belief.” Oregon linebacker Devon Jackson (#9) drops UCLA running back Wayne Knight (#3) for no gain as the No. 13 Ducks face the No. 21 Bruins in a Big Ten college football game at Autzen Stadium in Eugene on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. Sean Meagher/The Oregonian The Ducks, who host Nebraska (5-1, 2-1) at 8 p.m. Saturday, responded well to adversity following a 39-31 loss at Oklahoma State on Sept. 12. Oregon won its next two games, including a 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. That victory seemed to give the Ducks a fresh start. But two weeks later, they lost to the Bruins and dropped out of the rankings. Now, Oregon must run the table to have a legitimate shot at the College Football Playoff, which seemed like a given for a team that returned most of its starters from last year’s semifinal squad. item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon’s loss at Illinois and firing of OC Drew Mehringer
item.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — The Oregon Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) suffered their worst loss of the season at Illinois on Saturday . The 21-10 defeat came against a marginal Illinois team that started a true freshman at quarterback, rushed for 225 yards, and held Oregon to two scoring drives. As a result, on Sunday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning announced the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . What that means for the rest of the season remains to be seen. Mehringer had to contend with several key personnel issues, including starting quarterback Dante Moore missing three games while in concussion protocol. Here are 10 takeaways from Saturday’s game and the firing of Mehringer: 1. It feels like Mehringer is the scapegoat in this mess Criticizing play-calling is an armchair quarterback’s delight, but doing so under Oregon’s current circumstances is somewhat obtuse. Few teams excel without their starting quarterback. The next factor is an offensive line that was clearly mismanaged in the offseason after losing three starters to the NFL. Next is inconsistent play from backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Then sprinkle in losing top wideout Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot) after three games, starting wide receiver Evan Stewart (undisclosed injury) for the last two games, and two more rotational wide receivers heading into Illinois. Does all of that excuse Mehringer for Oregon scoring just 42 points over the past three weeks? No. But those are a lot of obstacles for any offensive coordinator to overcome. Watch " Oregon football fires offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer " on YouTube Watch 2. Where does Lanning go from here? Lanning will probably announce his new offensive coordinator during his Monday press conference. He could promote from within to get through the season and then conduct a national search in the offseason. Or he may have someone in mind to take over now and beyond. Whatever Lanning decides, the next play-caller had better hope Moore returns, or little will change. 3. It could be time to add a veteran coach to the staff Lanning did well by hiring younger offensive coordinators, Kenny Dillingham and then Will Stein. But maybe it’s time to bring in an accomplished, seasoned veteran coach to add a new perspective to a relatively young staff. Someone with a track record of success as an offensive coordinator and maybe as a head coach. Someone like former Oregon coach Chip Kelly, Northwestern’s offensive coordinator. No, don’t expect Kelly to want to return to Oregon. But someone like him could fit perfectly. 4. The wide receiver situation After Saturday’s game, Raiola was asked twice how difficult it was to build timing with the receiving crew, which lacked McClellan, Stewart, and freshmen Messiah Hampton and Jalen Lott. item.description: A new head coach will roam the sidelines. A franchise icon will make his long-awaited return. An All-Star will begin his redemption tour. And a new ownership group will watch its first season opener from Paul Allen’s former seats along the Moda Center baseline. The Blazers open the 2026-27 NBA season Wednesday night against the Phoenix Suns — a team they upset in April in the play-in tournament — and if you’re just now tuning in for the start of the regular season, well, there’s a lot you missed. The backcourt duo is joining a fivesome that includes returning starters Deni Avdija , Toumani Camara and Donovan Clingan . It’s a versatile, star-studded lineup that features three All-Stars, a former All-Defensive Second Team selection, one of the best young centers in the NBA and loads of scoring potential. item.title: Oregon QB Dante Moore ruled out for rest of 2026 season
item.description: Oregon Ducks quarterback Dante Moore will miss the rest of the season, coach Dan Lanning announced Monday night. “I’m not anticipating him being back this season,” Lanning said. “Really got clarity for us this past week, for him,” Lanning added. “And I think if it were up to Dante in any shape, way, he would want to be out there playing for the guys. But, unfortunately, it’s not really up to Dante. It’s not really up to me. We can control the setting and practice where he’s able to do things for us, but that’s not always the case in the game.” Lanning said he expects Moore, who has run scout-team offense in practice, to fully recover. “That hasn’t changed,” Lanning said. “Definitely feel that way, but for him to be out there on the field for us right now, that’s not gonna happen.” Lanning added that Moore would remain involved with the team. “He’s still going to be a big part of this team and helping us move forward and find opportunities for us to be better,” Lanning said. Watch " Oregon Ducks QB Dante Moore to miss remainder of 2026 season " on YouTube Watch The announcement comes days after the reeling Ducks lost 21-10 at Illinois on Saturday in the third straight game Moore missed while in concussion protocol. Before the Illinois game, Moore told The Oregonian/OregonLive that he felt good but didn’t know if he’d return this season and was taking it “one day at a time.” “That’s all I can do,” he said. Saturday’s loss all but knocked Oregon (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) out of the national playoff picture and led Lanning to fire offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer on Sunday. item.title: OSU's Legree leads nation in receiving as WSU clash looms
item.description: CORVALLIS — There may be no more appropriate way to describe Oregon State’s outrageously successful passing game this season than explosive. The Beavers lead the country in passing yards thanks in large part to 10 passes of 40-plus yards. Jesse Legree is responsible for eight of those catches, including all five of OSU’s 50-yard pass plays this season, making it no surprise that he leads the country in receiving yards and touchdowns entering this week’s matchup with Washington State. “You see him with ball in space, obviously taking the top off a number of times,” Washington State coach Kirby Moore said. “I think it’s about playing team defense. Obviously communication is going to be really important, where he’s at.” The Cougars (1-5, 0-2 Pac-12) have the No. 2 defense in the Pac-12 thus far and are having that success by keeping the top on their pass coverage. WSU has allowed 11 passes of 30-plus yards, which is tied for 129th nationally and nearly 10% of the passes it has allowed. However, opponents are not breaking through that mark often, with just four passes over 40 yards and none for more than 50, one of 30 teams yet to allow such a play this season. “We don’t want to let the verticals up,” Washington State safety Jaylen Smith said. “We take pride in (not) letting deep balls go. We always look to play top down and take away the deep routes first.” WSU defensive coordinator Trent Bray will be tasked with doing what nobody has been able to do yet this season: contain Legree. OSU offensive coordinator Mitch Dahlen has been creative in moving Legree around to prevent defenses from taking him away. Last week against San Diego State that included moving Legree into the backfield for a variety of plays. “People are going to try and hit him at the line of scrimmage,” Dahlen said. “They’re going to try and two-hand jam. If they’re going to try and two-hand jam, it’s like OK, how can I move this guy enough where you can’t do that? You put him in the backfield, unless you want to jump offsides and do it, you can’t do it that way. “That’s what we do a good job of as a staff, is moving him around where you can’t just put a safety over the top of him because if he’s in the backfield, what are you going to do there?” Even if the Cougars manage to limit Legree, the Beavers have shown they are more than capable of going elsewhere, with an outrageous 14 players catching passes last week. Aeryn Hampton (20 receptions for 245 yards) and tight ends Eric Olsen and DeCorion Temple each have at least 20 catches and Aaron Butler has four grabs for at least 20 yards. item.description: Dodgers Reportedly Have Free Agency Interest in Red Sox's Utility Man originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The focus for the Boston Red Sox at the moment is improving on both sides of the baseball, but they do have some of their own free agents who have to figure out what they want to do and where they plan on playing next season. One of those guys is Isiah Kiner-Falefa, who appeared in just 66 games throughout the year due to an injury and not having the biggest role. Kiner-Falefa has been in this league since making his debut in 2018 and has been a guy who can contribute at any given moment. He's not a perfect player by any means, but there's a reason why he keeps finding jobs year in and year out, specifically for contending teams. The former New York Yankees and Boston utility man shouldn't have a difficult time finding a job this winter, either. According to the latest report, the National League powerhouse Los Angeles Dodgers are interested in bringing in the 31-year-old. “Two more names on different ends of the scale have registered at least some level of interest from the Dodgers, a league source said: Mauricio Dubón and Isiah Kiner-Falefa. The source spoke anonymously because they were not authorized to speak publicly,” Fabian Ardaya wrote . The Hawaii native didn't have a bad year last season by any means in Boston, especially for the role that the Red Sox were hoping for him to fill. He came in and played decent defense, swung it at a somewhat competent level, and has largely been the player that he has been for much of his career. Kiner-Falefa isn't going to wow anybody offensively, posting an 81 OPS+ throughout his career, the same exact mark that he posted last year in Boston. However, he fills a couple of different roles defensively, so it wouldn't be surprising to see a team like the Dodgers end up signing him. item.title: Recap: OKC Blue can't get stops in 128-115 loss to Memphis Hustle
item.description: The OKC Blue couldn't put up video game numbers in a 128-115 loss to the Memphis Hustle on Thursday. The road defeat dropped their record to 0-3 in the 2026-27 G League regular season. It didn't take long for the Blue to fall behind by double-digit points. They were in a 32-26 deficit after the first quarter. Both teams picked up the scoring pace in the second frame — flirting with 40-point quarters. OKC had 34 points in it. But the Hustle did more as defense was optional. The Blue were in a 70-60 hole at the halftime break. Coming out of the halftime break, the Blue started to lose even more ground. They only had 22 points in the third quarter. That put them in a 101-82 deficit. By that point, OKC's defense was nonexistent. Memphis carved them up at all four levels — inside the paint, in the mid-range, outside the perimeter and at the free-throw line. The Blue sprayed perfume on the final score with 33 points in the final, but the game was already decided. They trailed by as many as 20 points. OKC couldn't cut it below double-digit points. There was no real threat of a comeback attempt. The Blue shot 45% from the field and went 15-of-37 (40.5%) from 3. They shot 12-of-17 on free throws. They had 21 assists on 39 baskets. Six Blue players scored double-digit points. Meanwhile, the Hustle shot 53% from the field and went 14-of-33 (42.4%) from 3. They shot 18-of-24 on free throws. They had 27 assists on 42 baskets. Five Hustle players scored double-digit points. item.title: Bagnaia Has Surgery On Fractured Right Foot
item.description: Photos by Ducati. The Ducati Lenovo Team confirmed Francesco Bagnaia successfully underwent surgery to repair the double fracture in his right foot sustained in the Sprint race at the Qatar GP. A medical team led by Dr. Luigi Milano at Turin's Humanitas Cellini Clinic secured a plate to his fourth metatarsal and stabilized the fifth, the two bones that run along the outer edge of the foot, leading to the little toe and its neighbor. The injury came on the opening lap of Saturday's Sprint, where Bagnaia went down in a highside crash following a collision with Fermin Aldeguer. Bagnaia was stretchered away and later diagnosed with the two fractures. Ducati says rehabilitation will start as soon as possible, and the days ahead will determine the timeline for a return to action. That leaves his participation in the final two rounds of the season in doubt. Typical recovery for a metatarsal fracture of this type runs around six weeks, though MotoGP riders have been known to come back sooner than the average person. Bagnaia is unlikely to be back for the November 20-22 Portugal GP, but it's possible he could line up at the Nov. 27-29 Valencia GP or, at the least, take part in the post-season Valencia test. If he does return for the test, it will be for a different manufacturer, as Bagnaia is leaving Ducati for Aprilia. A first proper run on the Aprilia RS-GP would do a lot for preparing for the 2027 season. It would allow him to turn the page on a disappointing 2026 that saw him fighting to feel settled and fast aboard the GP26. Bagnaia currently sits 9th overall, but fourth among Ducati riders, including his teammate, Marc Marquez, who is on the cusp of clinching his 10th world title. Whether or not he rides, Ducati would likely want to recognize Bagnaia's time with the factory team. Bagnaia won the 2022 and 2023 titles for Ducati, its first premier-class crown since Casey Stoner in 2007. Bagnaia was also the first Italian to win the championship for Ducati. item.title: Mason Miller wins NL Reliever of the Year
item.description: San Diego Padres closer Mason Miller was voted the National League Reliever of the Year for 2026. He received all 30 first-place votes from the members of the BBWAA. This is the first time the award has been given out. He also won the Trevor Hoffman National League Reliever of the Year Award, which is voted on by the relievers in baseball. That honor was also announced on Wednesday. Miller led all NL relievers with a 1.67 ERA in 66 appearances and 70 innings pitched. He also had the highest strikeout rate among NL relievers at 47.3%. Miller set new highs for workload in his first full season with the Padres and had one of the most dominant starts to a season ever seen in baseball. He didn’t allow a run until his tenth appearance, and it was unearned. His first earned run didn’t occur until his 14th appearance. During that stretch, he had a 61% strikeout rate. Miller was somewhat less effective at the end of the season and in the playoffs, probably due to the unprecedented workload. He expressed a desire to be better going forward, stating, “I saw my consistency falter toward the end of the year… just find a way to be even more consistent and put together a complete season.” Miller overcame significant obstacles during his remarkable season. He missed time with a family illness and bereavement, as well as leaving to attend the birth of his first child during the playoffs. Padres named to All-MLB First Team Padres closer Mason Miller and RF/2B Fernando Tatis Jr. were named to the All-MLB First Team on Wednesday. Major League Baseball presents the All-MLB First Team as part of their MLB Awards in Las Vegas. The award recognizes the best player at every position, including five starting pitchers and two relievers. Miller and Louis Varland of the Toronto Blue Jays were the two relievers honored. Tatis was named for his work in the outfield, along with Pete Crow-Armstrong of the Cubs and Jackson Chourio of the Brewers.

Through his first 10 games, James has struggled with his offensive efficiency, particularly away from the rim, as evidenced by his 11-point outing in Tuesday’s 123-101 home loss to the Boston Celtics. According to the analyst, James’ waning production could put an asterisk next to the final chapter of his storied career. Rob Parker Questions LeBron James’ Impact on 76ers Speaking on Wednesday’s edition of “The Odd Couple,” Parker sounded the alarm on James’ rough start. “If you look at the numbers, okay, against Boston, 4-for-12, 11 points, 8 rebounds, 5 assists. Last week against the [Cleveland Cavaliers], he had twice as many turnovers than baskets in that game. On the season, averaging 15, 7, and 6 on 43/23/70, it’s the worst he’s shot from the field since his rookie season,” Parker said. “… He shot 38% or worse in four of the 10 games so far.” READ MORE: ‘Looking Like He’s Lost a Step,’ ‘I Hate It’ — Ex-Knicks Guard Urges LeBron James To Consider Early Retirement After Getting Posterized by Jayson Tatum James shot just 3-for-12 (25%) and committed 6 turnovers in Friday’s 119-95 road loss to the Cavaliers. Between those losses, James had a better showing, scoring 22 points on strong 8-for-16 shooting (50%) in Sunday’s 127-121 road win over the Chicago Bulls. Still, his averages are well below what fans have come to expect after he earned his record-extending 22nd All-Star selection with the Los Angeles Lakers last season. item.description: The University of Akron is headed to the Big East Conference men's soccer tournament championship. Akron dominated Creighton 4-0 in a tournament semifinal on Thursday, Nov. 12, at the Maryland SportsPlex in Boyds, Md. Jack Sullivan, Jack Roman, Remi Agunbiade and Londen Sears each scored a goal for No. 3 seed Akron (12-1-4), which topped No. 2 Creighton (12-2-5) after the two teams played to a 1-1 draw in the regular season. Akron will meet No. 1 seed Georgetown (15-1-2) in the championship match at 2 p.m. Sunday, Nov. 15. It will be televised on ESPNU. Georgetown was a 2-0 winner over No. 4 seed Seton Hall (7-5-6) in Thursday's other semifinal at the Maryland SportsPlex. Akron , ranked No. 4 in the country in the coaches poll, has won five matches in a row and seven of its past nine since losing 3-1 at home to Georgetown on Sept. 25. The Hoyas were ranked No. 5 in the country then and are now No. 2 behind top-ranked Southern Methodist University. Akron men's soccer scores three goals in opening 10 minutes to beat Creighton The Zips scored three goals in a span of 2 minutes and 59 seconds during the opening 10 minutes of Thursday's match to separate from the Bluejays. Sullivan opened the scoring in the seventh minute after Thomas O'Rourke chipped the ball into the penalty box area. Sullivan received the pass and took an off-balance shot with his right foot to slot the ball into the net. Roman netted his goal just under 90 seconds later when he took two dribbles before sending a shot with his right-foot into the upper-right corner. Tyler Morck and Sullivan were credited with assists. Akron extended its lead to 3-0 in the 10th minute. Matt Dreas delivered a long ball from approximately 40 yards out toward the left side of the penalty area, where Roman brought it down just inside the box and then passed it to a cutting Agunbiade, who right-footed the ball into the net. Akron entered halftime with an advantage in shots (9-3), shots on goal (6-1) and corner kicks (4-0). "We came out fast," Akron coach Jared Embick said during an interview at halftime with ESPN+ broadcasters. "The adrenaline was hot, and we took advantage." The Zips added a fourth goal in the 85th minute to conclude the scoring. Nolan McGuire played the ball to Ignacio Alem, who advanced down the sideline before sending a low pass across the penalty area. Londen Sears received the pass and tapped the ball into the net. Akron finished with an edge in shots (12-5), shots on goal (7-1) and corner kicks (8-2). Akron goalkeeper Brett Kaminski recorded one save and Creighton's Matthew Hudson finished with three saves. item.title: Red Wings Fall Apart Against Panthers to Choke Away Three Goal Lead
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect On the wrong end of a four game losing skid that started after the Red Wings left Amerant Bank Arena after beating the Florida Panthers earlier this month, the Red Wings came back to Sunrise and beat themselves, losing a three goal lead to fall 5-4 in regulation. The Panthers opened scoring after Sam Reinhart squeaked a shot in past John Gibson ‘s armpit when the Red Wings couldn’t counter Florida’s rush. However, JT Compher tied things up 15 seconds later with a breakaway goal after Carter Mazur , in for Michael Rasmussen , collected the puck along the boards mid-ice before flipping it to Compher to take the puck the rest of the way home past Akira Schmid. Detroit would score the next three goals, with Andreas Englund and Lucas Raymond both getting tip ins off of Panthers defenseman Seth Jones in the first and second periods respectively. Marco Kasper would score his first goal of the season in his second game back from injury to put the Red Wings up 4-1 a little over halfway through regulation. However, Detroit couldn’t put the game away tonight. After putting up four goals over the first 59 minutes of the game, the Red Wings let in four unanswered over the next 21 minutes. Gustav Forsling started the Panthers comeback after scoring in the closing minute of the second period. Michael Brandsegg-Nygård was called for high-sticking on Matthew Tkachuk to start the third period, and the Panthers would capitalize as time expired on the following power play. Anton Lundell drew the Panthers within one off of Carter Verhaeghe’s shot when Gibson fell trying to reach out and cover the puck. Lars Eller batted the puck in over Gibson’s shoulder with 3:31 left in regulation to tie things up. Lundell would put his second goal past Gibson less than a minute later to give the Panthers a 5-4 lead, and ultimately the win. Takeaways Detroit has now lost its fifth game in a row, this time coughing up a three goal lead on the way to the loss. While the Red Wings offense came alive tonight in the first half of the game, their defensive effort and attention to detail clearly slipped in the second half, allowing the Panthers to get under their skin to come back for the win. Key Stat Detroit has fourteen goals in their last six games. Nine of them have come in their two games against the Panthers, and tonight, the Red Wings weren’t able to win with four goals and the lead, and are now on a five game losing streak. Key Moment The Panthers, who had been itching for a fight and looking for energy found some life when Forsling pulled the Panthers within 2 with just 18 seconds left in the second frame. The Red Wings simply could not stop the bleeding once it started, and let the next three goals go in unanswered.
